at_1pct_fpr.note: Nearly a tie: ~19k alerts is deep enough that both models have found 92-93% of the fraud. This view understates the difference.

reading: Both models eventually find most fraud; GraphSAGE finds it EARLIER in the ranking. At a fixed 1% FPR the confusion matrices converge, but at a realistic review budget GraphSAGE catches 1.7-1.8x the fraud for identical analyst effort. Rank quality, not a different decision boundary, is what the 86% AUC-PR gain buys.
caveat: The GraphSAGE threshold was chosen at the target FPR on the replay's own 2019 scores, while XGBoost's came from val. Both landed at 0.99% FPR so the 1% FPR comparison is fair in practice, but the clean comparison is the matched-budget one, which involves no threshold at all. Picking the GNN threshold from a causal replay of 2018 would remove the asymmetry.
